scenarios.name: enters-and-empowers-jace-one
scenarios.why: When it enters with no Jace token around, its trigger creates a blue Jace planeswalker token with one loyalty counter. The runner locates tokens by printed face name (the token's CR 111.4 name is 'Jace Token'), so the ref is p0:token:Token; the Jace subtype is asserted separately.

scenarios.name: jace-token-uses-granted-plus-two
scenarios.why: Planeswalkers its controller controls have '[+2]: This planeswalker deals 1 damage to each opponent and you gain 1 life.' The Jace token activates it: loyalty 1 -> 3, the opponent goes to 19 and its controller to 21.

scenarios.name: zero-loyalty-token-survives-until-lurker-leaves
scenarios.why: The Jace token's [-1] takes it to 0 loyalty. While Sanctum Lurker is on the battlefield, its controller's planeswalkers aren't put into the graveyard for having 0 loyalty, so the token stays. Once the Lurker leaves (moved to the graveyard), the CR 704.5i state-based action applies at the next check (CR 704.3: whenever a player would receive priority; the runner's move op is an outside stand-in, so a pass gives the engine that check) and the token is gone.

scenarios.name: nontoken-walker-protected-opponents-is-not
scenarios.why: Lightning Bolt takes its controller's Liliana of the Veil to 0 loyalty: she stays (Lurker's static covers every planeswalker its controller controls, not just Jace tokens) and can then use the granted [+2] (0 -> 2, opponent 19, controller 21). The opponent's Jace Beleren bolted to 0 loyalty is NOT protected and goes to its owner's graveyard.
